title: useEffect Revision Notes: Deps, Cleanup, Fetching and When Not to Use It
summary: Quick night-before notes on React's useEffect: what it is for, how dependency arrays and cleanup work, fetching safely with race-condition guards plus loading and error states, and how to avoid effects you don't need.

chapters.title: What useEffect Is and the Mental Model
points: Definition: useEffect(setup, deps?) synchronizes a component with an external system (network, DOM API, timer, subscription); it is not a lifecycle hook
Timing: the effect runs after React commits and the browser paints, so it never blocks rendering; useLayoutEffect is the pre-paint variant for measuring layout
Think 'synchronize', not 'on mount': each render has its own effect closure that sees that render's props and state
Use an effect only for things caused by the component being displayed (fetch on show, subscribe, set up a listener); things caused by a user action belong in the event handler
Interview Point: Why does useEffect run after paint? What is the difference between useEffect and useLayoutEffect? Is useEffect a componentDidMount replacement?

chapters.title: Dependency Arrays
points: Three forms: no array runs after every render; [] runs once after mount; [a, b] runs after mount and whenever a or b changes (compared with Object.is)
Rule: list every reactive value the effect reads (props, state, values derived in the component); never silence react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
Objects, arrays and functions created in the component body are new on every render, so as deps they re-fire the effect every time; move them inside the effect, outside the component, or memoize them
Use the functional updater setCount(c => c + 1) to drop a state value from deps, and read the latest value through a ref when the effect must not re-run
Interview Point: What happens if you omit a dependency (stale closure)? Why does an object in deps cause an infinite loop? How does React compare dependencies?

chapters.title: Cleanup Functions and Strict Mode
points: Return a function from the effect to undo its setup: removeEventListener, clearInterval, unsubscribe, abort a request
Order: on a dep change React runs the previous effect's cleanup (with the old values), then the new effect; cleanup also runs on unmount

Strict Mode in development mounts, unmounts and remounts once to expose missing cleanup; the effect always runs twice in development, and if the visible result differs from a single run (two timers, two connections) the cleanup is missing or wrong, so fix the cleanup rather than the double run
Example: useEffect(() => { const id = setInterval(tick, 1000); return () => clearInterval(id); }, [])
Interview Point: When exactly does cleanup run? Why does my effect run twice in development? What leaks if you skip cleanup on a subscription?

chapters.title: Fetching Data: Race Conditions, Loading and Error States
points: Race condition: when id changes quickly, an older, slower response can arrive last and overwrite the newer result
Fix with an ignore flag: let ignore = false; fetch().then(d => { if (!ignore) setData(d) }); return () => { ignore = true }
Better fix with AbortController: pass signal to fetch, call controller.abort() in cleanup, and ignore the AbortError in the catch

Model request state as loading, error and data: set loading true and error null at the start, handle res.ok (fetch does not reject on 404 or 500), and set loading false in finally only if the request was not aborted (if (!controller.signal.aborted)), so a cancelled request cannot clear the newer request's loading state
Interview Point: How do you prevent a stale response from overwriting a newer one? Does fetch reject on HTTP 500? Why use TanStack Query or SWR instead of a hand-rolled fetch effect?

chapters.title: Avoiding Unnecessary Effects and Common Mistakes
points: Derived data: compute it during render (const full = first + ' ' + last), or useMemo if it is expensive, instead of useEffect plus setState, which causes an extra render
Responding to a user action (submit, click, POST): do it in the event handler, not in an effect watching state
Resetting state when a prop changes: give the component a key (<Profile key={userId} />) instead of an effect that calls setState

Mistakes: async function passed directly to useEffect (it returns a Promise, not a cleanup; define an inner async function and call it), missing cleanup, an effect that sets state it also depends on (infinite loop)
Interview Point: Name three cases where you don't need useEffect. Why can't the effect callback be async? How do you reset state when a prop changes?

chapters.title: useEffect Cheat Sheet
points: Deps: none runs every render, [] runs on mount only, [x] runs when x changes; list everything reactive and trust the lint rule
Cleanup: return a function; it runs before the next effect and on unmount; Strict Mode double-run is a cleanup test
Fetch recipe: AbortController or ignore flag, loading/error/data state, check res.ok, set loading false in finally unless the request was aborted
Skip the effect for derived values (compute in render), user actions (event handler) and prop-driven resets (key)
Interview Point: Walk through a safe fetch-on-prop-change effect from scratch. When is useEffect the wrong tool?
